encounters.name: The applauding dead

locked: Function: Deepen the apparent-heir interpretation through true but curated memories.
Moral question: Is a useful public story worth preserving when the evidence does not fully support it?
open: When the wight falls the play begins without it: a traveller arrives by sea, a gate opens, a crowd cheers (EC-AM-04). The traveller is addressed only as 'the one who came.'
Kaelra calls the play a prophecy; Selric asks who chose which scenes to keep.

original.does: The theater's last master of ceremonies in a steward's chain; still runs the performance, and points the audience at anyone who interrupts it.

languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak
original.does: The audience in rotted finery, applauding a play no one performs; rise and shamble at whoever the wight points to.

routes.when: A character steps onto the stage and performs before the wight points.
routes.success: The wight is delighted: an actor at last. It bows, the audience applauds, and the play begins with the performer in it. The dead sit and watch; no one fights while the play lasts.
routes.failure: The wight hisses at the poor show and points: the audience rises.
lines: Wight: 'Places! Places! The one who came is late again.'
routes.reveals: The performer is cast as 'the one who came' and walks the scenes; the scenes the play leaves out are the ones that would complicate it.
routes.canon: Delivers the function: true memories, curated.

routes.when: A character addresses the wight as the steward it was, by its chain of office, before the applause stops.
routes.success: The wight answers as a steward: the performance was ordered 'until the true successor sees it', and it will hold the house until the end. It lets the party watch from the tiers.
routes.failure: It takes the party for hecklers and has them removed.
lines: Wight: 'I was told to keep the story. I was never told it was finished.'
routes.reveals: The play was commanded, and someone chose its scenes.
routes.canon: Sets up the moral question: who keeps a useful story, and why.
